arxiv-2107-07209.title: Aspects of the polynomial affine model of gravity in three dimensions Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2107-07209.creator: Oscar Castillo-Felisola addr1,e1, Oscar Orellana addr2, José Perdiguero addr1, Francisca Ramírez addr1, Aureliano Skirzewski addr3, Alfonso R. Zerwekh addr1
arxiv-2107-07209.description: Abstract The polynomial affine gravity is a model that is built up without the explicit use of a metric tensor field. In this article we reformulate the three-dimensional model and, given the decomposition of the affine connection, we analyse the consistently truncated sectors. Using the cosmological ansatz for the connection, we scan the cosmological solutions on the truncated sectors.

arxiv-2109-06503.title: Beam halo from Touschek scattering in the KEK Accelerator Test Facility
arxiv-2109-06503.creator: R. Yang 1,2, A. Aryshev 1,2 , P. Bambade 3 , M. Bergamaschi 4 , K. Kubo 1,2 , T. Naito 1,2 , N. Terunuma 1,2 , S. Wallon 3, J. Zhang 5
arxiv-2109-06503.description: Abstract Beam halo is one of the crucial issues limiting the machine performance and causing radioactivation in high-intensity accelerators. A clear picture of beam-halo formation is of great importance for successful suppression of the undesired beam loss. We present numerical and experimental studies of transverse and longitudinal halos in the KEK Accelerator Test Facility.

arxiv-2209-00634.title: A (Co)Algebraic Framework for Ordered Processes Thanks: This work was partially supported by ERC grant Autoprobe (grant agreement 101002697).
arxiv-2209-00634.creator: Todd Schmid
arxiv-2209-00634.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Todd Schmid. A recently published paper [ 1 ] offers a (co)algebraic framework for studying processes with monadic branching structures and recursion operators. The framework captures Milner’s algebra of regular behaviours [ 2 ] , but fails to give an honest account of a closely related calculus of probabilistic processes [ 3 ] We capture Stark and Smolka’s calculus by giving an alternative framework, aimed at studying a family of ordered process calculi with inequationally specified branching structures and recursion operators.

arxiv-2210-10185.title: An Adaptive Hybrid Control Algorithm for Sender-Receiver Clock Synchronization
arxiv-2210-10185.description: Abstract This paper presents an innovative hybrid systems approach to the sender-receiver synchronization of timers. Via the hybrid systems framework, we unite the traditional sender-receiver algorithm for clock synchronization with an online, adaptive strategy to achieve synchronization of the clock rates to exponentially synchronize a pair of clocks connected over a network.

arxiv-2309-09210.title: The U ​ ( 1 ) L μ − L τ U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}} breaking phase transition, muon g − 2 g-2 , dark matter, collider and gravitational wave
arxiv-2309-09210.creator: Jie Wang, Jinghong Ma, Jing Gao, Xiao-Fang Han ∗ , Lei Wang
arxiv-2309-09210.description: Abstract Combining the dark matter and muon g − 2 g-2 anomaly, we study the U ​ ( 1 ) L μ − L τ U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}} breaking phase transition, gravitational wave spectra, and the direct detection at the LHC in an extra U ​ ( 1 ) L μ − L τ U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}} gauge symmetry extension of the standard model.

arxiv-2506-20399.title: Multimodal Behaviour Trees for Robotic Laboratory Task Automation
arxiv-2506-20399.creator: Hatem Fakhruldeen, Arvind Raveendran Nambiar, Satheeshkumar Veeramani, Bonilkumar Vijaykumar Tailor, Hadi Beyzaee Juneghani, Gabriella Pizzuto, Andrew Ian Cooper
arxiv-2506-20399.description: Abstract Laboratory robotics offer the capability to conduct experiments with a high degree of precision and reproducibility, with the potential to transform scientific research. Trivial and repeatable tasks; e.g., sample transportation for analysis and vial capping are well-suited for robots; if done successfully and reliably, chemists could contribute their efforts towards more critical research activities.

arxiv-2511-02247.creator: Hao Li, Daiwei Lu, Jesse d’Almeida, Dilara Isik, Ehsan Khodapanah Aghdam, Nick DiSanto, Ayberk Acar, Susheela Sharma, Jie Ying Wu, Robert J. Webster III, Ipek Oguz

Webster III, Ipek Oguz. Monocular depth estimation (MDE) is a critical task to guide autonomous medical robots. However, obtaining absolute (metric) depth from an endoscopy camera in surgical scenes is difficult, which limits supervised learning of depth on real endoscopic images.

pmc-10621960.title: Histological evaluation of the distribution of systemic AA-amyloidosis in nine domestic shorthair cats
pmc-10621960.creator: Valentina Moccia, Anne-Cathrine Vogt, Stefano Ricagno, Carolina Callegari, Monique Vogel, Eric Zini, Silvia Ferro, Khaled Abd EL-Hamid Abd EL-Razik, Khaled Abd EL-Hamid Abd EL-Razik, Khaled Abd EL-Hamid Abd EL-Razik
pmc-10621960.description: Amyloidosis is a group of protein-misfolding disorders characterized by the accumulation of amyloid in organs, both in humans and animals. AA-amyloidosis is considered a reactive type of amyloidosis and in humans is characterized by the deposition of AA-amyloid fibrils in one or more organs. In domestic shorthair cats, AA-amyloidosis was recently reported to be frequent in shelters.

pmc-11437137.title: Heme deficiency in skeletal muscle exacerbates sarcopenia and impairs autophagy by reducing AMPK signaling
pmc-11437137.creator: Takeru Akabane, Hiromori Sagae, Koen van Wijk, Shinichi Saitoh, Tomohiro Kimura, Satoshi Okano, Ken Kodama, Kiwamu Takahashi, Motowo Nakajima, Tohru Tanaka, Michiaki Takagi, Osamu Nakajima
pmc-11437137.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Heme serves as a prosthetic group in hemoproteins, including subunits of the mammalian mitochondrial electron transfer chain. The first enzyme in vertebrate heme biosynthesis, 5-aminolevulinic acid synthase 1 (ALAS1), is ubiquitously expressed and essential for producing 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA). We previously showed that Alas1 heterozygous mice at 20–35 weeks (aged-A1+/−s) manifested impaired glucose metabolism, mitochondrial malformation in skeletal muscle, and reduced exercise tolerance, potentially linked to autophagy dysfunction.

pmc-11478077.title: Surface Tension of Cu-Ti Alloys and Wettability in a Liquid Alloy–Refractory Material-Gaseous Phase System
pmc-11478077.creator: Katarzyna Nowinska, Grzegorz Siwiec, Tomasz Matula, Alphonce Wikedzi, Beata Oleksiak, Jaroslaw Piatkowski, Tomasz Merder, Mariola Saternus, Piotr Piszczek, Jun Liu
pmc-11478077.description: The study involved measurements of surface tension of liquid binary copper-titanium alloys with respect to their chemical composition and temperature as well as investigations of the liquid alloy–refractory material-gaseous phase system wettability using usual refractory materials, i.e., graphite, aluminum oxide and magnesium oxide.

pmc-11490246.title: Recombinant Keratin-Chitosan Cryogel Decorated with Gallic Acid-Reduced Silver Nanoparticles for Wound Healing
pmc-11490246.creator: Nanan Miao, Tao Jiang, Yuanchao Li, Sihong Xue, Shilei Hao, Chunli Zhou, Yujie Gu, Ran Li, Bo Yu, Xiaoqu Duan, Wenchao Xu, Rupeng Wang, Lei Ran
pmc-11490246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundWound healing is a complex physiological process that can be roughly divided into four stages: hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and remodeling. Conventional wound dressings often fail to meet the diverse needs of these healing stages due to their limited functionality. Cryogels, however, possess several attractive properties, such as large, interconnected pores, good mechanical strength, and ease of modification, making them suitable for developing advanced dressings with multiple functions.

pmc-11498145.title: Introducing S.C.O.P.E.™ (Schizophrenia Clinical Outcome Scenarios and Patient–Provider Engagement), an Interactive Digital Platform to Educate Healthcare Professionals on Schizophrenia Care
pmc-11498145.creator: Christoph U Correll, Jose M Rubio, Leslie Citrome, Marko A Mychaskiw, Stephen Thompson, Kelli R Franzenburg, Mark Suett, Sameer Kotak, John M Kane
pmc-11498145.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Despite evidence of benefits beyond those of oral antipsychotics, long-acting injectable antipsychotics (LAIs) are underused in schizophrenia treatment. Underuse may be partially a result of misconceptions held by some healthcare professionals (HCPs) pertaining to LAIs. A panel of four experts convened between January 2022 and May 2022 to identify these misconceptions, and example cases or scenarios were created to illustrate common clinical situations relevant to these beliefs.

pmc-11631991.title: Variability in resistance training trajectories of breast cancer patients undergoing therapy
pmc-11631991.creator: Maximilian Koeppel, Karen Steindorf, Martina E. Schmidt, Friederike Rosenberger, Joachim Wiskemann
pmc-11631991.description: PurposeIn resistance training (RT), the change in volume-load from training sessions (TS) to TS is an indicator of training progress. Resulting growth trajectories are likely to differ between individuals. Understanding this variation is important for exercise planning in general, but even more for clinical populations. We investigated this variation in breast cancer patients undergoing treatment.

pmc-13147269.title: Causal effect of school-entry age on long-run family formation: Quasi-experimental evidence from 14 million individuals in Vietnam
pmc-13147269.creator: Ishaan Busireddy, Janny Liao, Dat Hoang Vu, Tam Ngo Minh Tran, Jan-Walter De Neve
pmc-13147269.description: School-entry age has been suggested to affect human capital development. Little is known, however, about the impacts of school-entry age on long-run outcomes, particularly in lower-income countries where most children and adolescents worldwide reside. We exploit a natural experiment based on school-entry rules in Vietnam to examine the causal effect of school-entry age on educational outcomes and family formation.

pmc-13454785.title: Revaluation of Granadilla (Passiflora ligularis): Analysis of Phenolic Compounds and Their Antioxidant Activity
pmc-13454785.creator: Fabiola N Cuyo-Jallasi, Harry R Yucra-Condori, Miriam D Hubinger, Julio C Rodríguez-Díaz, Poulami Jha
pmc-13454785.description: This study is aimed at evaluating the effect of solvents such as ethanol and methanol on the extraction of phenolic compounds with antioxidant capacity from granadilla (Passiflora ligularis). Extraction was assisted with ultrasound (40 kHz, 30°C). The sample‐to‐solvent ratio was 1:14, and extraction was performed separately for seeds and peels.

pmc-13609499.title: Phase-Separation-Engineered Porous Polyimide Fibers via Wet Spinning for Superior Thermal Insulation
pmc-13609499.creator: Ruihong Sun, Fujuan Liu
pmc-13609499.description: Personal thermal management (PTM) textiles can reduce building energy consumption and improve personal comfort, yet their practical application is constrained by the inherent trade-off between flexibility, thermal insulation, and mechanical strength. Herein, porous single-component polyimide (PI) fibers were fabricated via coagulation bath-modulated wet spinning of 3,3′,4,4′-benzophenone tetracarboxylic dianhydride (BTDA)–4,4′-oxydianiline (ODA) poly(amic acid) (PAA).

pmc-13643448.title: Smartphone-Measured Sleep Health Risk Factors Detect Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors Among Adolescents
pmc-13643448.creator: Jaclyn S Kirshenbaum, David Pagliaccio, Esha Trivedi, Hanga Galfalvy, Karla J Joyce, Katherine Durham, Giovanna Porta, Paul A Bloom, Trinity C Tse, Ashley Blanchard, Lauren S Chernick, Ryann N Crowley, Peter S Dayan, Lauren E Kahn, Jamie Zelazny, David A Brent, Nicholas B Allen, Randy P Auerbach
pmc-13643448.description: ObjectiveSuicide deaths and poor sleep health in adolescents have significantly increased. Smartphone sensors (eg, accelerometry) provide an unobtrusive and scalable way to monitor sleep health over extended time periods. We hypothesized that poor weekly sleep health (ie, shorter and variable time in bed; late and variable bedtime) assessed through smartphone sensors would associate with weekly suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB).
